# Escape while the grid's edit dialog opens skips its focus return

Owned: my #21727 exposed it, and its fix follows today; not offered to contributors.

## Context

Since #21727 landed on `dev` (`b10c77bdbe`), `test/playwright/e2e/grid/EditInDialogExample.spec.mjs` › "opens and closes by keyboard, discards on Escape, …" fails now and then in CI: `dev`'s push run 44872058346 (`e2e-engine (12/15)`) and #21732's run 44871811594 (`e2e-engine (2/15)`).

```
Error: expect(locator).toBeFocused() failed
Locator:  locator('.neo-grid-row').first().locator('.neo-button').filter({ hasText: 'Edit' })
Expected: focused
Received: inactive
```

Locally it failed once in 36 runs. Pressing Escape right after the dialog's First Name field takes focus leaves focus off the Edit button 5 of 5 times on `dev` `07b6cbd213`.

## The Problem

#21727 makes a dialog take focus into its first field as it mounts, so a person, or the test, can press Escape while the open animation still runs, while the dialog is in its mount flight. The example's dialog then never sends focus to its Edit button.

A focus trace of that Escape on `dev` (main thread, ms from the first focus):

```
5    in  neo-button-4
9    key Enter on neo-button-4
20   out neo-button-4 to neo-grid-view-1
76   in  neo-textfield-1__input from neo-grid-view-1
108  key Escape on neo-textfield-1__input
383  removed neo-dialog-1
383  in  neo-grid-view-1 from null
```

Enter on the Edit button moves focus to the grid view before the dialog opens, so focus enters the dialog from the view, and the dialog's own hand-back (#21415) returns it there once the dialog is removed. The example sends focus on to its Edit button from its `hide()` override, but only on `hide(false)`, which `animateHide()` calls at its end. A hide while the dialog still opens takes `component.Base#hide()` at once and never makes that call.

Before #21727 the same Escape was possible, but the test only pressed it after the example focused First Name on `show`, after the animation.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: "A departing `dialog.Base` hands focus back to its opener: the component focus came from, else `animateTarget`, through the existing `restoreFrom` hand-back, so a focus the user has moved elsewhere stays." (#21415, The Fix, item 3). The trace shows it working: focus returns to the grid view, where it came from.

- `dialog.Base#hide()` animates out only when mounted and out of its mount flight; otherwise `component.Base#hide()` leaves the removal to the flight.
- `dialog.Base` fires `hide` once on every path: at once when it cannot animate, and at the end of `animateHide()` otherwise.
- `examples/grid/nestedRecordFields/EditUserDialog.mjs` focuses its `animateTarget` from a `hide()` override keyed on its `animate` argument.

## The Fix

The example's dialog names its opener first in `getFocusReturnTarget()` (`this.animateTarget || super.getFocusReturnTarget()`), so the engine's departure hand-back (#21415) focuses the Edit button as the dialog leaves the DOM, on every hide path; its `hide()` override goes. A test presses Escape right after the dialog opens and expects focus on the row's Edit button, taken once, after the dialog has left the DOM.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Escape while the dialog still opens hands focus back to the Edit button, only once the dialog has left the DOM (a new e2e, red on `dev`'s example).
- [ ] The keyboard test of `EditInDialogExample.spec.mjs` passes 20 runs in a row locally.

## Out of Scope

- Enter on a button in a grid cell moving focus to the grid view: a defect-note of its own.
- The engine's hand-back (#21415), which returns focus where it came from.

## Avoided Traps

- Handing focus back at the start of `dialog.Base#hide()`, as `close()` does: tried; it returns focus to the grid view sooner, no closer to the button, and changes every dialog.
- Focusing the opener from the dialog's own `hide` event: #21757's first head. An early hide fires it while the dialog is still in the DOM, so the Edit button behind the modal took focus about 275 ms before the removal (Sophie's trace on #21757).
- Waiting in the test for the open animation to end: it would hide a focus loss a person can cause.
